title: Ontology-Guided KG-RAG for Geoscientific Knowledge and Reasoning
subtitle: Connecting scientific literature, structured knowledge and reasoning
question: Can structured domain knowledge improve the reliability and scientific usefulness of AI reasoning in geohazard research?
context: Scientific literature on geomaterials, swelling and shrinkage, environmental triggers, hydrological response, crack evolution, hydro-mechanical instability, monitoring, prediction, mitigation and risk management.
progress: Ongoing research organizes domain knowledge and source evidence to support retrieval and scientific reasoning.
direction: Can Scientific AI jointly reason over data, physics and knowledge?
next: Improve evidence traceability and the alignment of generated conclusions with retrieved scientific sources.
update: The 26 August 2026 report describes an ontology-guided knowledge framework built from 536 full-text papers, evaluated using 170 domain questions and an expansive-soil landslide case. These are progress-report materials, not a claim of publication.
outputs: Ontology, knowledge organization and evaluation are ongoing. Public paper, code and data are forthcoming.
